chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al-Halaby, who said:

I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about the Hajj, so he said: 'Perform Tamattu'. Then he said: 'When we stand before Allah, Exalted and Majestic, we say: O Lord, we held fast to Your Book and the Sunnah of Your Prophet, while the people say: We acted according to our own opinions.'

key_terms.تَمَتَّعْ: Tamattu (a type of Hajj combining Umrah and Hajj)
key_terms.رَأَيْنَا بِرَأْيِنَا: We opined with our opinions (reliance on personal judgment)

ai.seo_question: What is the difference between how the Imams and the general people present their case before God on the Day of Judgment?
ai.summary: In this hadith from al-Kafi, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) prescribes the Hajj al-Tamattu and uses it as a springboard to highlight a fundamental epistemological divide: the Ahl al-Bayt's adherence to the objective revelation of the Quran and Sunnah versus the general populace's reliance on subjective reasoning (ra'y). This contrast underscores the Shia principle that true guidance stems from divine text and its infallible interpreters, rather than human opinion, a theme central to Shia usul al-fiqh.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al Halby who said,

‘I asked Abu Abdullahasws about the Hajj, so heasws said: ‘Tamatto (تَمَتَّعْ)’. Then heasws said: ‘Weasws, when weasws pause in front of Allahazwj Mighty and Majestic (on the Day of Judgement), weasws would say: ‘O Lordazwj! We took with Yourazwj Book and Sunnah of Yourazwj Prophetsaww’, and the people would say, ‘We opined with our opinions’.
en.sarwar: 8. Ahmad ibn Muhammad from has narrated from Ali ibn Hadid who has said the following: “Once Ali ibn Muyassir wrote to him (the Imam) asking about a man who performed al-‘Umrah in the month of Ramadan, then it was al-Hajj season; if he could perform al-Hajj as al-Mufrid al-Hajj or al- Hajj al-Tamattu‘ (advantageous), and which one was better.
He (the Imam) wrote in answer, ‘Al-Hajj al-Tamattu‘ is better.’”
